title: Decoder and demap method selection in DVB-T2 AWGN campaign runner
description:
Add CLI selection of the LDPC belief-propagation decoder algorithm and the QAM soft-demap method to the DVB-T2 BICM AWGN campaign runner, so the campaign can be tuned toward the ETSI reference instead of being locked to plain min-sum with max-log demapping.

## Background

The campaign runner (`crates/gf2-coding/src/bin/dvb_t2_awgn_campaign.rs`) previously hardcoded `DemapMethod::MaxLog` and used the `DvbT2Concat` default LDPC decoder, which is plain `DecoderAlgorithm::MinSum`. A calibration smoke run showed this default configuration sits roughly 1.0–1.5 dB above the ETSI TS 102 831 QEF thresholds at the bracketing SNR points — exceeding the campaign's $\le 0.5$ dB gap target. Normalized-min-sum (or sum-product) decoding plus exact log-MAP demapping recover most of that gap. Both decoder variants and both demap methods already exist in the codebase; only the runner lacked a way to select them.

## Success Criteria

- [ ] [hard] The campaign binary accepts `--decoder` (values `minsum`, `nms:ALPHA`, `oms:BETA`, `sumproduct`) and `--demap` (values `maxlog`, `exactlogmap`), parsing each into the corresponding `DecoderConfig` / `DemapMethod`, with a clear error on unrecognized values.
- [ ] [hard] The selected demap method is used by the BICM channel (no hardcoded `MaxLog`), and the selected decoder configuration is applied to the `DvbT2Concat` codec before decoding.
- [ ] [hard] `DvbT2Concat` exposes a way to override its LDPC decoder configuration that rebuilds the decoder with the supplied algorithm.
- [ ] [hard] Omitting both flags preserves prior behavior (`minsum`, `maxlog`), so existing artefacts and resume byte-identity are unaffected.

## Notes

- This capability was implemented during an AWGN-campaign session as a prerequisite for meeting the campaign's gap target; it is tracked as its own task because the campaign simulation issue is execution-only and forbids new code.
